questions.text: Give a comparative discussion about alphabet, language, and power on alphabet.

Give the formal definition of Deterministic Finite Automata (DFA). Design a DFA that accepts the following language L over the alphabet $\{0,1\}$.

$L=\{ w \mid w \text{ has contains the symbol 1 at most three times}\}$

Also give the transition diagram of that DFA.
Write down the properties of Nondeterministic Finite Automata (NFA). How can you test the membership of a string? Use example.
Define $\epsilon$-NFA. Draw an $\epsilon$-NFA that searches KUET and STUDENT from a test document.
Convert the following NFA into DFA using subset construction method.

figures.alt: Fig. 2(b): NFA with states 0 (start), 1 and 2 (accepting, double circle). State 0 has a self-loop labelled a,b and goes to 1 on b. State 1 goes to 2 on b. State 2 has a self-loop labelled a,b.

questions.text: Convert regular expression $(a+b)b^*(a+b)^*$ to an $\epsilon$-NFA. Show the steps. Also Describe the extended transition function $\hat{\delta}$ for $\epsilon$-NFA with suitable example.

Let M be the DFA having alphabet $\{a, b\}$ and the following transition diagram:

Give a regular expression for L(M). Try to keep your expression simple. (Use any method you want)

figures.alt: DFA over {a,b} with states 1 (start), 2 (accepting) and 3 (accepting), both drawn as double circles. State 1: self-loop b, a to 2. State 2: self-loop b, a to 3. State 3: self-loop b, a to 1.

questions.review_note: Arrow directions on the scanned diagram (2-a->3 and 3-a->1) read as the only assignment that gives each state one a and one b transition; 2 and 3 are both double circles in the photo.

questions.text: What is Kleene Closure of a language? Find $L^2$ and $L^3$ of the language $L=\{1, 01\}$.

Write regular expression/definition for the following languages:

- (i) All strings containing no more than three a's over alphabet $\{a, b, c\}$
- (ii) The set of strings of 0's and 1's whose number of 0's is divisible by three and whose number of 1's is odd.
- (iii) All string of digits with at most one repeated digit.
- (iv) All Strings which contain no runs of a's of length greater than two over alphabet $\{a, b, c\}$
State pumping lemma. Using pumping lemma, show that the language of palindrome is not regular.
Design a Context Free Grammar (CFG) for the language $\{ X^aY^bZ^c \mid a=b \text{ or } b \neq c, \text{ where } a, b, c \ge 0 \}$

Define ambiguous grammar. Use string aabbb to find out whether the following grammar is ambiguous or not. If yes, give an equivalent unambiguous grammar.

$$\begin{aligned}
S &\to BS \mid \epsilon \\
B &\to Bb \mid aBb \mid ab
\end{aligned}$$

Define Push Down Automata (PDA). Construct push down automata for the following languages. Acceptance either by empty stack or by final state.

- (i) $L=\{a^nb^n \mid n \ge 0\}$
- (ii) Equal number of 0's and 1's.
For PDA, distinguish between acceptance by final state, and by empty tack.
Prove that "If L be $L(P_F)$ for some PDA $P_F$ where $P_F = (Q,\Sigma,\Gamma,\delta_F,q_0,z_0,F)$ then there is a PDA $P_N$ such that $L = N(P_N)$".
Define instantaneous description of a Turing Machine (TM). What is the role of checking off symbols in TM?
Design a Turing Machine (TM) M to implement the function "Subtraction". Simulate the action for the input 00000100.

Convert the following grammar to a PDA that accepts the same language by empty stack.

$$\begin{aligned}
S &\to 0S1 \mid A \\
A &\to 1A0 \mid S \mid \epsilon
\end{aligned}$$

Simulate the action for the input 0011 on the new PDA.

Define Chomsky Normal Form (CNF). Find a grammar in CNF equivalent to

$$\begin{aligned}
S &\to aAbB \\
A &\to aA / a \\
B &\to bB / b
\end{aligned}$$

Consider the following grammar

$$\begin{aligned}
S &\to a \mid aA \mid B \mid C \\
A &\to aB \mid \epsilon \\
B &\to Aa \\
C &\to cCD \\
D &\to ddd
\end{aligned}$$

and simply safe order

- (i) Eliminate $\epsilon$-production.
- (ii) Eliminate Unit Productions.
- (iii) Eliminate Useless Symbols.
- (iv) Put the grammar into CNF.
State Pumping lemma and its advantages?

Show that the following languages are not context-free:

- (i) $L=\{w \in \{a,b,c\}^* : w \text{ has equal numbers of a's and b's and c's}\}$
- (ii) $L=\{a^nb^ma^n : n \ge m\}$
Prove that context free languages are closed under (i) Homomorphism (ii) Reversal
Define DPDA. Let $\Sigma=\{0, 1\}$, consider the problem of testing whether a PDA accepts some string of the form $\{ w \in 0^*1^* \}$. Is this problem decidable? Prove your answer.
